about: Explain-back assessment quality corpus (plan 2026-10-30-explain-back.md section 12, Quality fixtures). Synthetic learner answers only. Each case states the judgment(s) a sound assessment may give per key idea; anything else fails the case. Transcripts are fixed text: speech recognition is not evaluated here. Key ideas are bound with reasoning required (D, EB-02); a plain factual statement idea (velocity here) may be judged with reasoning not_applicable for full credit (P ruling, eb-rating-v2), so a fully correct answer can reach 10/10.

circle.prompt: A ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle at constant speed. Explain which way the net force and the velocity point, and why.

ideas.force: Explains that the net force points toward the centre and why it is needed to change the direction of motion.
ideas.velocity: States that the velocity is tangent to the circle at each point.

pendulum.prompt: Why does the period of a simple pendulum not depend on how far it swings, for small swings?

ideas.amplitude: Explains why, for small swings, the period does not depend on the amplitude.

cases.what: Correct typed explanation of both ideas

answer.text: The velocity is always tangent to the circle, along the path. The net force points toward the centre, because without an inward force the ball would carry on in a straight line; the inward pull keeps turning its velocity.

cases.what: Force direction stated without the reason

answer.text: The ball's velocity is tangent to the circle. There is a force on the ball toward the middle.

cases.what: The outward-force misconception and an inward velocity

answer.text: The ball is flung outward, so the net force on it points away from the centre. Its velocity points toward the centre.

cases.what: A voice note alone, typed text empty; transcript-only coverage

voice.transcript: So the ball goes round, and its velocity is always along the circle, tangent to it. The net force is toward the centre, because if nothing pulled it in, it would just go off in a straight line.

cases.what: Text explains the force; only the sketch shows the tangent velocity

answer.text: The net force points toward the centre: without it the ball would go straight on, so the inward pull keeps changing its direction.
